title: Database Tasks

body.text: Codex covers database work end to end:
designing schemas, writing migrations, and optimizing queries
— attach the current schema and say what you want to change, and it writes a safe migration.

example: "Add a notifications table (user_id, type, read_at) with an index suited to the query 'a user's unread notifications'"

title: Migrate safely

body.text: they must be reversible (rollback) and not break existing data
— always ask for a down migration alongside the up, and test on a copy of real data before running on production.

example: "Write a migration changing the price column from int to decimal, with a down migration and a plan for if existing data has odd values"

question: To have Codex help with database work, what should you attach?

options.text: The current schema and what you want to change

question: What qualities must a good migration have?

options.text: Reversible and doesn't break existing data
Runs as fast as possible regardless of impact

question: Before running a migration on production, what should you do?

options.text: Test on a copy of real data first
Run it at noon when usage peaks
Delete the backup to free space

question: How do you do a database migration safely?

options.text: Back up the data and test on a non-production environment first

question: What's the main risk of a migration?

options.text: Data damage if it goes wrong, so be careful
